entries.answer: A mother is the female parent, and the word reaches well past biology, so a mother church, a mother country and the mother of a movement all mean origin rather than parenthood. That extension is the usual translation mistake, because Tagalog ina and amay are narrower, and Bisaya mama and ina likewise. English also distinguishes the two lines by prefix, so maternal grandfather is the mother's father, not simply any grandfather.

entries.answer: A father is the male parent, and like mother it generalises to origin and authorship, as in the father of modern chemistry or the father of the company. The extension creates a genuine ambiguity in reading, because the father of the theory may mean the person who originated it rather than a parent at all. English pairs it with mother, grandmother and grandfather, and adds the adjectival forms paternal and maternal to separate the two lines.

entries.answer: A sibling is a brother or a sister, and the word exists in English precisely because there is no single unmarked term for someone who shares a parent. Brother and sister are the everyday words and each marks gender, while sibling is the neutral one used on forms, in records and in general statements. The relationship needs at least one shared parent, so half-siblings qualify, and step-siblings do not, since none is shared.

patterns: is there a word for gender of cousin
entries.answer: A cousin is a child of an aunt or uncle, and English uses the same word at every generational distance, unlike its other kin terms, which are sharply marked by age. First cousins share a grandparent, and the children of first cousins are first cousins once removed, with removed counting the generations between. There is no separate word for gender, and none for a cousin's own child, which is the opposite of how English handles uncle against aunt.

patterns: what do you call a step grandmother
entries.answer: A grandparent is a parent of a parent, giving grandmother and grandfather, and English extends the pair to great-grandparents and then abandons the counting. The unmarked word grandparent is neutral while the two marked ones are not. What is missing is any term at all for the spouse of a grandparent, so a stepfamily has to borrow or invent vocabulary for that person, which is one of the clearest places English kinship naming runs out.

entries.answer: A child is a person below the age of adulthood, and the word also means the result of anything, as in a child of the marriage. Older usage meant son or daughter, so a legal document writing children of the king means the royal offspring specifically, a sense surviving mainly in formal and historical writing. The plural is irregular, and child and children behave unlike any other pair in the language, which is why they are learned as an exception.
